# A history read off its finite stretches

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`a-history-read-off-its-finite-stretches` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](a-history-read-off-its-finite-stretches.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> For every process, its histories are the ideals of the order of its finite stretches. Adhering is the least closed class; refutable and closed classes pass into each other up to a step that, asked of every process, is exactly double-negation elimination.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. An ideal of a preorder of stretches is a nonempty set of stretches, closed downward, in which any two are extended by a third; ideals are ordered by inclusion, and two holding the same stretches are the same history (antisymmetry is not used). A principal ideal is a finite history. (`Becoming.Ideals.Preorder`, `Becoming.Ideals.Ideal`, `Becoming.Ideals.Ideal.LE`, `Becoming.Ideals.Ideal.Same`, `Becoming.Ideals.idealOrder`, `Becoming.Ideals.principal`, `Becoming.Ideals.principal_le_iff`)
2. For a process, a stretch is a run with a horizon, one extending another where its horizon is later and the two runs agree up to the earlier. A run is the ideal of the stretches it passes through; two runs' ideals lie one below the other exactly where the runs agree at every horizon, and no run's ideal is a finite history. (`Becoming.stretchOrder`, `Becoming.Run.stretches`, `Becoming.Run.stretches_le_iff`, `Becoming.Run.stretches_not_principal`)
3. A reading of points is refutable where every point outside it has a stretch that no point of the reading passes through, and a point adheres to it where each of its stretches is a stretch of a point of the reading. (`Becoming.Ideals.RefutableBy`, `Becoming.Ideals.AdheresBy`)
4. A refutable reading holds, up to double negation, at every adhering point; a refutable superset so holds at every point adhering to the subset; where the reading is stable adhering is holding; and a point adhering while outside shows the reading is not refutable. (`Becoming.Ideals.RefutableBy.not_not`, `Becoming.Ideals.RefutableBy.adheres_least`, `Becoming.Ideals.RefutableBy.adheres_iff`, `Becoming.Ideals.not_refutableBy_of_adheres`, `Becoming.Ideals.refutableBy_adheres_iff`)
5. For runs these are refutability and adherence at the runs' ideals, so the laws of Becoming.Horizon on what a finite history refutes follow from them as their case of runs. (`Becoming.refutable_iff_refutableBy`, `Becoming.adheres_iff_adheresBy`, `Becoming.Refutable.not_not`, `Becoming.Refutable.adheres_least`, `Becoming.Refutable.adheres_iff`, `Becoming.not_refutable_of_adheres`, `Becoming.refutable_adheres_iff`)
6. A class of ideals is closed where it is closed downward and under directed unions. It is closed exactly where it is the class of the ideals within a lower set of stretches; that set is unique and is the class's content, the stretches of its ideals. (`Becoming.Ideals.ScottClosed`, `Becoming.Ideals.Lower`, `Becoming.Ideals.Within`, `Becoming.Ideals.Content`, `Becoming.Ideals.closed_iff_within_principal`, `Becoming.Ideals.closed_iff_lower`, `Becoming.Ideals.lower_unique`, `Becoming.Ideals.lower_iff_content`, `Becoming.Ideals.content_lower`)
7. On runs, a reading holding every run adhering to it is the reading of the runs whose stretches lie in the content of its runs: it is made of tests, one for each stretch, read as propositions. A run lies in a closed class exactly where each of its stretches is a stretch of a history of the class. (`Becoming.closed_iff_within_lower`, `Becoming.Stretches.closed_runs`)
8. The hull of a class, the ideals each of whose stretches is a stretch of an ideal of the class, is its least closed superclass: closed, holding the class, unique, adding no stretch, and joint, any two stretches of an ideal of the hull being extended by one stretch of one ideal of the class. (`Becoming.Ideals.Hull`, `Becoming.Ideals.AdheresBy.of`, `Becoming.Ideals.hull_closed`, `Becoming.Ideals.hull_least`, `Becoming.Ideals.hull_content`, `Becoming.Ideals.hull_unique`, `Becoming.Ideals.hull_joint`)
9. On runs, a run adheres to a reading exactly where its ideal lies in the hull of the reading's runs, that is, in every closed class of histories holding them, with no double negation. (`Becoming.runClass`, `Becoming.adheres_iff_hull`, `Becoming.Stretches.adheres_iff_closed`, `Becoming.Stretches.adherence_unique`, `Becoming.Stretches.adheres_content`, `Becoming.Stretches.adheres_joint`)
10. A refutable class is closed up to double negation, and a closed class is refutable where a history known not to lie within it shows a stretch outside. Asked of every order and class, each step is exactly double-negation elimination. (`Becoming.Ideals.Refutable`, `Becoming.Ideals.Refutable.closed`, `Becoming.Ideals.ScottClosed.refutable_iff`, `Becoming.Ideals.within_refutable_iff`, `Becoming.Ideals.refutable_closed_iff`, `Becoming.Ideals.closed_refutable_iff`)
11. Asked of every process, each step is again exactly double-negation elimination, with witnesses on the process of (): not being refuted by any finite stretch is not belonging, and a history known not to lie within a closed class does not thereby show the stretch at which it leaves. (`Becoming.Stretches.unitCut`, `Becoming.Stretches.refutable_closed_iff`, `Becoming.Stretches.closed_refutable_iff`)
12. A refutable class of histories is refutable at runs, and asked of every process a refutable reading holds at every run adhering to it exactly under double-negation elimination. (`Becoming.Stretches.refutable_of_class`, `Becoming.Stretches.within_refutable`, `Becoming.refutable_holds_iff`)
13. The ideals avoiding a set of stretches form a closed class, the only closed class holding exactly the finite histories that avoid the set, and refutable where every ideal failing to avoid it holds a stretch of it; on runs, a run adhering to the runs that avoid the set avoids it. These are the safety classes. (`Becoming.Ideals.Avoids`, `Becoming.Ideals.avoids_iff_within`, `Becoming.Ideals.avoids_closed`, `Becoming.Ideals.avoids_unique`, `Becoming.Ideals.avoids_refutable_of_found`, `Becoming.Stretches.avoids_adheres`, `Becoming.Stretches.avoids_runs`, `Becoming.Stretches.avoids_refutable`)
14. A lower set of stretches, with the order it inherits, has as its ideals exactly the ideals within it, by lifting and restricting, the order kept; on runs, the histories of the set's order are the process's histories within it, and two runs within it are ordered there exactly where they agree at every horizon. (`Becoming.Ideals.Preorder.restrict`, `Becoming.Ideals.Ideal.restrict`, `Becoming.Ideals.Ideal.lift`, `Becoming.Ideals.lift_within`, `Becoming.Ideals.lift_restrict`, `Becoming.Ideals.restrict_lift`, `Becoming.Ideals.lift_le_iff`, `Becoming.Stretches.inherited_histories`, `Becoming.Stretches.within_order_iff`)
15. The ideals are directed-complete, and the compact ones are exactly the finite histories. A monotone map of stretches into a directed-complete order extends to a continuous map of ideals, unique up to the target's equivalence; a compact basis that generates fixes its completion up to an equivalence the basis fixes; and the readings "lies above this stretch" tell ideals apart. (`Becoming.Ideals.DirectedComplete`, `Becoming.Ideals.idealComplete`, `Becoming.Ideals.Compact`, `Becoming.Ideals.compact_iff_principal`, `Becoming.Ideals.Monotone`, `Becoming.Ideals.Continuous`, `Becoming.Ideals.extend`, `Becoming.Ideals.unique_continuous_extension`, `Becoming.Ideals.CompactBasis`, `Becoming.Ideals.OrderEquivalence`, `Becoming.Ideals.principal_basis`, `Becoming.Ideals.unique_basis_representation`, `Becoming.Ideals.above`, `Becoming.Ideals.extend_above_iff`, `Becoming.Ideals.above_readings_separate`)
16. On runs: no run is compact; a continuous reading of the histories is fixed at every run by its values on finite histories; finite stretches tell runs apart; the finite histories are a compact basis, and the histories are the completion of the stretches. (`Becoming.Stretches.run_not_compact`, `Becoming.Stretches.run_reading_unique`, `Becoming.Stretches.runs_told_apart`, `Becoming.Stretches.finite_basis`, `Becoming.Stretches.histories_representation`)
17. A history settles where one of its stretches reaches the latest horizon among them, and goes on where it has stretches beyond every horizon. One that settles is a finite history; one that goes on, with a stretch beyond each horizon picked, is the history of the run read off the picks. (`Becoming.Stretches.HasLatest`, `Becoming.Stretches.GoesOn`, `Becoming.Stretches.hasLatest_principal`, `Becoming.Stretches.pickedRun`, `Becoming.Stretches.goesOn_run`)
18. So, for every process, a history that settles, or goes on with its stretches picked, is a finite history or a run; a finite history settles and a run's history goes on. (`Becoming.Stretches.classification`, `Becoming.Stretches.principal_hasLatest`, `Becoming.Stretches.run_goesOn`)
19. Telling, of every history of the process of () cut at a Boolean sequence's first true, whether it settles or goes on is exactly the limited principle of omniscience: telling whether a history ends is deciding whether it changes again. (`Becoming.Stretches.cut`, `Becoming.Stretches.cut_decided_iff_lpo`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.cut`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.cut_decided_iff_lpo`)
20. Words are ordered by prefix; a sequence is the ideal of its initial words. A history, finite or infinite, has an ideal below another's exactly where it is a prefix of it, and the same words make the same history; an ideal of words that settles, or goes on with its words picked, is a history. For the process of all sequences the runs' histories are these, in order, sameness and prefix-closed languages. (`Becoming.HistoryIdeals.prefixOrder`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.traceIdeal`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.History`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.historyIdeal`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.history_le_iff`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.historyIdeal_same_iff`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.classification`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.sequence_stretch_iff`, `Becoming.Stretches.sequences_le_iff`, `Becoming.Stretches.sequences_same_iff`, `Becoming.Stretches.sequences_within_iff`)
21. A prefix-closed language is a lower set of words, so its histories form a closed class; the finite histories with the infinite histories of a property are not refutable where some sequence lies outside it, recurrence among them. (`Becoming.HistoryIdeals.prefixClosed_iff_lower`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.history_within_iff`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.FiniteOr`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.finiteOr_not_refutable`, `Becoming.HistoryIdeals.finiteOr_recurs_not_refutable`)
22. Instance (periphery, own checker): the completion package's IdealWarrant, CompletionRole and HistoryIdeals read as instances, a poset's order the core's order of stretches and its ideals, classes, content and hull the core's. (`Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.toCore`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.finiteRefutable_iff_refutable`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.scottClosed_iff_closed`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.scottHull_iff_hull`)
23. W1's Scott closure as a lower basis, W2's least hull and W2a's prohibitions as an avoiding basis follow with empty axiom reports; W1's equivalence of finite refutability and Scott closure, A2, A2a, A3 and A4 follow with the classical and extensionality steps each needs named. (`Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.scottClosed_iff_lower_basis_by_core`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.hull_least_by_core`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.respects_iff_admits_avoiding_by_core`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.finiteRefutable_iff_scottClosed_by_core`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.unique_continuous_extension_by_core`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.positive_reading_membership_by_core`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.unique_basis_representation_by_core`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.ideal_classification_by_core`, `Becoming.IdealsCorrespondence.history_order_iff_by_core`)
24. The word half on the courses a process can take: an ideal of courses feasible from a configuration that settles, or goes on with a course of each length picked, is a history of the process from there (one feasible course, or a sequence of moves each of whose initial courses is feasible); a feasible course settles; a run's moves go on, each initial course the trace of its first steps. (`Becoming.HistoryIdealsTraces.HistoryOf`, `Becoming.HistoryIdealsTraces.classification`, `Becoming.HistoryIdealsTraces.course_settles`, `Becoming.HistoryIdealsTraces.run_initial_trace`, `Becoming.HistoryIdealsTraces.run_goesOn`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. The order is any preorder (antisymmetry is not used, so the same history is two-way inclusion); the process and the readings are arbitrary. The classification takes the decision of settling and the picked stretches as data.
- Double-negation elimination is the hypothesis of one direction of refutable_closed_iff, closed_refutable_iff and refutable_holds_iff, and the limited principle of omniscience of one direction of cut_decided_iff_lpo. The instance module uses Lean's standard axioms where its declarations name them.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Which readings of an actual unfolding are refutable or closed: that depends on the process they are read on; the laws say what each gives.
- That every refutable class is closed, or every closed class refutable, without a decision: asked of every process each is exactly double-negation elimination. Witness: `Becoming.Stretches.refutable_closed_iff`.
- That every history settles or goes on: asked of the cut histories of the process of () it is exactly the limited principle of omniscience. Witness: `Becoming.Stretches.cut_decided_iff_lpo`.
- Boolean tests from the propositional tests a closed reading is made of: that needs each stretch's test decided (compare refutable_passes_iff_markov).
- **Counterexample:** On the process of (), the histories passing through the stretch at horizon 1, or all where a proposition holds, are refutable once it is not refuted, and closed only if it holds (refutable_closed_iff); the histories within the stretches at horizon 0 are closed, and the history reaching horizon 1 where the proposition holds shows no refuting stretch unless it holds (unitCut, closed_refutable_iff). The finite histories with the infinite histories of a property are not refutable (finiteOr_not_refutable). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/HistoryIdeals.lean)
- **Counterexample:** A history of feasible courses need not be a run's moves: from no configuration the countdown goes to any count and then counts down, so every course of ()s is feasible from there, and no run starts there (history_without_run). [source](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/HistoryIdealsTraces.lean)

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise is used. The core declarations use no Lean axiom; the periphery declarations cited use only Lean's standard axioms (propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice), as their receipts report. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Decision D45 (4) joined IdealWarrant with CompletionRole and HistoryIdeals as one core family under structural names (board item A4-L). Ren, 19 October 2026: “integrate all, the theory is a whole, not stitched pieces, go ahead” (provenance, not warrant); his “(a)” of 16 October had kept IdealWarrant outside the spine (study section 153). The ideals of the order of finite stretches are the ideal completion of domain theory (Abramsky and Jung 1994); on runs the closed classes are the safety properties of Alpern and Schneider (1985), and refutation from finite data is that of Kelly (1996), as what-a-finite-history-refutes notes. Classically finite refutability and Scott closure coincide (IdealWarrant's W1); constructively each direction is a step that, asked of every order and class, is exactly double-negation elimination. Readings (the AI's): not being refuted by any finite stretch is not belonging; a history known not to lie within a closed class does not thereby show the stretch at which it leaves; telling whether a history ends is deciding whether it changes again.

<a id="dependencies--依赖"></a>
### Dependencies

- **formal-reuse**: [what-a-finite-history-refutes](what-a-finite-history-refutes.md). Reuses Becoming.Horizon's Run.AgreeUpTo, Refutable and Adheres: the order of stretches is agreement up to the earlier horizon, and Horizon's laws are the case of runs of the laws of points, which Becoming.Horizon proves them from (R26).
  - Output: Agreement up to a horizon, and refutability and adherence of readings of runs.
  - Input: The order of stretches, and the readings of runs the laws of ideals are read on.
  - Preserved conditions: None. [Horizon.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Horizon.lean)
- related, not a proved adapter: [becoming-finite-horizon](becoming-finite-horizon.md). There no finite prefix decides the whole-run classification in Renewable; here what a finite stretch refutes in every process, as the closed classes of its histories.
- related, not a proved adapter: [what-a-finite-stretch-verifies](what-a-finite-stretch-verifies.md). What a finite stretch verifies, the open classes dual to the closed classes here, and the split of every reading into its hull and a remainder no stretch refutes.
